follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $89.30 came from Premium and $10.70 from ads. Direct costs took $72.39 and running costs $22.99, finance items added $0.17 and tax was a $0.63 benefit, leaving $5.42 kept as profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.0811 (ECB euro reference rate at Mar 28, 2024). As reported: revenue €3,636M · gross profit €1,004M · operating income €168M · net income €197M.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago (+21% constant currency)

oneTimers: Operating expenses included €82M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price — versus €12M a year ago, and the charges came in €74M above forecast as the share price rose.

Finance costs of €53M included a €35M fair-value loss on the Exchangeable Notes as the share price rose, plus an €8M loss on derivative liabilities — largely offset by €45M of interest income, leaving finance items at a net +€6M.
The quarter carried a €4M impairment charge on real estate assets, part of the efficiency actions started in late 2023.

The quarter carried a €23M income tax benefit on €174M of pre-tax income — a -13.0% effective tax rate — driven by a €64M deferred-tax benefit from the unrealized gain in Spotify's Tencent Music investment, partly offset by €26M of tax expense from using share-based compensation deductions, versus a €19M tax expense a year ago.
otherDetail: Finance items netted +€6M — €59M of finance income, mostly €45M of interest income on the growing cash pile plus €8M of foreign-exchange gains, against €53M of finance costs, including a €35M fair-value loss on the Exchangeable Notes and €8M on derivative liabilities. A year ago finance items netted -€50M.

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 239 million people paying monthly, up 14% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.55, up 5% (+7% in constant currency) as price rises outweighed product mix; gross margin 30.2%.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue grew 18% (19% in constant currency) on double-digit growth across all regions; its gross margin rose to 6.4% as podcast and music profitability improved.

takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 27.6%, up 243 bps YoY, on better music and podcast profitability and lower other costs of revenue — gross profit passed €1 billion for the first time in Spotify's history. Premium gross margin reached 30.2% and Ad-Supported swung to a 6.4% gross margin from a loss a year ago. Operating income hit a record €168M, a 4.6% margin, versus a €156M loss a year ago.
takeaways.title: Record profitability

takeaways.text: Monthly active users grew 19% to 615 million — 13 million net additions in the quarter, though 3 million below guidance as marketing was moderated — with growth across all regions, led by Latin America and Rest of World. Premium subscribers rose 14% to 239 million, in line with guidance, and ad-supported users grew 22% to 388 million.
takeaways.title: Users kept growing

takeaways.text: Free cash flow was €207M, bringing trailing-12-month free cash flow to €828M and the cash pile to €4.7B. Net income swung to €197M from a €225M loss a year ago. Guidance for Q2 2024: 631M users, 245M subscribers, €3.8B revenue, 28.1% gross margin and €250M operating income.
takeaways.title: Cash piled up

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 20% to €3.64B (about $3.9B) and posted a record quarter — gross margin of 27.6% and operating income of €168M, both records — as 615 million monthly users and 239 million paying subscribers each grew double digits, swinging net income to €197M from a €225M loss a year ago.
